events.title: Australia Wage Price Index Climbs 1.1% In Q3
events.description: Australia's wage price index was up a seasonally adjusted 1.1 percent on quarter in the third quarter of 2026, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Wednesday.

events.title: Taiwan Stock Market May Give Up Support At 40,000 Points
events.description: The Taiwan stock market has finished lower in two consecutive trading days, tumbling almost 3,600 points or 8.6 percent. The Taiwan Stock Exchange now sits just above the 40,090-point plateau and it may open under pressure again on Wednesday.

events.title: Japan October Trade Shortfall Y476.5 Billion
events.description: Japan posted a merchandise trade deficit of 476.5 billion yen in October, the Ministry of Finance said on Wednesday.

events.title: Singapore Stock Market May Open Under Pressure On Wednesday
events.description: The Singapore stock market has moved lower in four straight sessions, retreating more than 175 points or 3.4 percent along the way. The Straits Times Index now sits just above the 5,100-point plateau and it may spin its wheels again on Wednesday.

events.title: Soft Star Expected For Malaysia Stock Market
events.description: The Malaysia stock market headed south again on Tuesday, one day after ending the five-day losing streak in which it had dropped more than 55 points or 3.3 percent. The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index now sits just above the 1,575-point plateau and it may take further damage on Wednesday.

events.title: Japan Stock Market May Extend Losing Streak
events.description: The Japan stock market has finished lower in two straight sessions, sinking almost 2,300 points or 3.8 percent in that span. The Nikkei 225 now sits just above the 58,860-point plateau and it's likely to extend those losses on Wednesday.

events.title: KOSPI May See Continued Consolidation
events.description: The South Korea stock market has finished lower in four straight sessions, slumping more than 400 points or 7.8 percent along the way. The KOSPI now sits just beneath the 4,970-point plateau and it may remain stuck in neutral on Wednesday.

events.title: Indonesia Rate Decision On Tap For Wednesday
events.description: The central bank in Indonesia will wrap up its monetary policy meeting on Wednesday and then announce its decision on interest rates, highlighting a modest day for Asia-Pacific economic activity.

events.title: Swiss Market Ends Sharply Lower
events.description: The Switzerland stock market closed notably lower on Tuesday, in line with most of the markets across Europe, as uncertainty about sustainability of AI trade and rising geopolitical tensions rendered the mood bearish.

events.title: European Stocks Fall Amid Nvidia Concerns, Middle East Tensions
events.description: European markets tumbled to multi-week lows Tuesday following reports the U.S. plans tighter restrictions on advanced AI chip exports to China. The Stoxx 600 fell 0.81%, while France's CAC 40 dropped 0.92% amid political concerns and Nvidia earnings anticipation.

events.title: Canadian Market Down 0.77% As Tech, Financials Weigh
events.description: Canada's S&P/TSX Composite Index fell 276.72 points to 35,445.41 on Tuesday amid technology sector pressure, inflation concerns, and potential monetary tightening. Tech stocks declined 2.5%, with Blackberry down 7%.

events.title: U.S. Business Inventories Climb 0.5% In September, In Line With Estimates
events.description: The Commerce Department released a report on Tuesday showing business inventories in the U.S. increased in line with economist estimates in the month of September. The report said business inventories climbed by 0.5 percent in September after rising by 0.4 percent in August.

events.title: U.S. Homebuilder Confidence Extends Slump, Hitting New 14-Year Low In November
events.description: Reflecting high mortgage rates, ongoing inflation pressure, elevated costs, rising labor shortages and hesitant buyers, the National Association of Home Builders released a report on Tuesday showing an extended slump in U.S. homebuilder confidence in the month of November.
